comment: What the read-only guards protect, for every lane and every runtime.
Read by setup/guards/deny_repo_writes.py (Claude Code and Codex) and
for specialists_from. Why each value is what it is stays in the comment
beside the readers; this file carries values.
Paths: a leading ~ is the user's home from the password database, not
$HOME, so a process that exports another HOME does not move what is
protected. specialists_from is the exception: the roster has always
product_repos is the floor: every lane protects every entry, plus its
own repo and worktrees. worktree_roots is the ONLY key that grants an
exemption (the spent-worktree teardown); a lane without it cannot reach
one. Adding a root here is a decision about every lane. git_tail and
redirect_tail fall back to defaults. A missing or malformed file makes
every guard REFUSE, it does not let anything through.

defaults.git_tail: The brainer is read-only there — only the task's executor changes repo state, in its own worktree. Read-only git (log/status/diff/show/rev-list) is allowed.
defaults.redirect_tail: If you were only reading and the '>' is part of a search pattern, keep the tree's absolute path out of the command. This check resolves the redirect's actual target — expanding `$HOME`/`~`, unwinding `..`, and following symlinks — before deciding, so respelling the path does not change the answer; it does not key on the literal text.

brain.where: a product repo or a live worktree

setup.where: the app repo or a live worktree
